title: ⚡️ Optimize dependency graph flattening
body:
## Summary

Replace recursive dependency-graph flattening with an iterative preorder traversal.

The previous implementation constructed a flattened subtree at each dependency level and copied that subtree into every ancestor. It also used linear list membership when skipping repeated dependencies.

This change:

- accumulates dependencies directly into one flat result;
- uses set-backed repeated-dependency detection, while retaining compatibility with unhashable callables;
- replaces recursive OAuth scope analysis with iterative postorder traversal;
- avoids recursion-limit failures for deeply nested dependency graphs;
- preserves dependency order, inherited OAuth scopes, parameter fields, and `skip_repeats` behavior.

This affects route construction and OpenAPI generation, not per-request dependency execution.

## Complexity

For a dependency chain of depth `d`, the previous recursive implementation repeatedly copied descendant lists into their ancestors, resulting in `O(d²)` work and memory references.

The iterative implementation traverses the dependency graph and accumulates the flattened result directly, making a chain `O(d)`.

For repeated dependencies, set-backed membership changes duplicate detection from `O(n²)` to average `O(n)` for hashable dependency cache keys. The list fallback preserves support for unhashable callables.

## Internal representation

The root flattened `Dependant` retains the same preorder dependency sequence and combined parameter fields.

One internal detail changes: entries in the root flat dependency list no longer retain their own recursively flattened descendant lists. All descendants are accumulated directly in the root flat list. Existing FastAPI consumers operate on the root flat collections.

## Benchmarks

A local synthetic benchmark flattening a 500-node dependency chain with `skip_repeats=True` measured:

| Implementation | Time |
|---|---:|
| `master` | ~7.8 ms |
| This PR | ~1.6 ms |

This is approximately a 4.9× improvement for that case.

The PR adds a focused CodSpeed benchmark so CI can provide the authoritative comparison across revisions.

Related discussion: #16057

title: Fix SSE data payload dropping trailing newlines
body:
### Summary

`format_sse_event` splits the data payload with `str.splitlines()` before writing each `data:` field. This silently drops a **trailing** newline, so a `ServerSentEvent` whose data ends in `\n` is sent one field short and a client reconstructs the payload without its final newline.

`str.splitlines()` also treats characters as line breaks that the SSE wire format does **not** recognize (`\v`, `\f`, `\x1c`–`\x1e`, `\x85`, ` `, ` `), so those characters inside `raw_data` — documented as sent "as-is" — get wrongly split into separate `data:` fields.

### Reproduction

```python
from fastapi.sse import format_sse_event

format_sse_event(data_str="line1\n")
# actual:   b'data: line1\n\n'          -> client rebuilds "line1"  (trailing "\n" lost)
# expected: b'data: line1\ndata: \n\n'  -> client rebuilds "line1\n"

format_sse_event(data_str="a\x0bb")
# actual:   b'data: a\ndata: b\n\n'     -> "\x0b" turned into a line break
# expected: b'data: a\x0bb\n\n'         -> "\x0b" sent as-is
```

Per the [WHATWG event-stream format](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#event-stream-interpretation), a stream is split into lines on **CR LF, CR, or LF only**, and a `data:` value is joined back with `\n` on the client. To transmit `"line1\n"` the server must emit `data: line1` followed by an empty `data:` field.

### Fix

Split the payload on the SSE line terminators (`\r\n`, `\r`, `\n`) and keep the trailing empty field, instead of using `str.splitlines()`. Multi-line data, CR, and CRLF continue to encode exactly as before.

A unit test covering the trailing-newline, empty, multi-line, CR/CRLF, and non-SSE-separator cases is added. `fastapi/sse.py` stays at 100% coverage.

title: 🐛 Fix `exclude_defaults` not propagated to dict keys and values in `jsonable_encoder`
body:
## Problem

`jsonable_encoder` forwards `exclude_defaults` when recursing into list/tuple/set items, but drops it when recursing into dict keys and values — while the sibling flags `exclude_unset` and `exclude_none` *are* forwarded in that same dict branch. The same model with the same flag encodes differently depending on its container:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder

class M(BaseModel):
    a: int = 5

jsonable_encoder([M()], exclude_defaults=True)       # [{}]
jsonable_encoder({"k": M()}, exclude_defaults=True)  # {"k": {"a": 5}}  <- flag silently ignored
```

Reproduced on 0.139.2.

## Fix

Forward `exclude_defaults` in the dict branch's key and value recursion, matching the list branch and the two sibling flags already passed there.

This deliberately does **not** change `include`/`exclude` propagation for dict values — that's the broader design question tracked in discussion #15961; this PR only removes the inconsistency between the two container branches for a flag that is already documented as recursive.

## Tests

Added `test_encode_model_with_default_in_dict_and_list` covering list, dict, and dict-of-list nesting plus a guard that `exclude_unset`/`exclude_none` behaviour is unchanged.

`pytest tests/test_jsonable_encoder.py tests/test_serialize_response.py tests/test_serialize_response_model.py tests/test_serialize_response_dataclass.py tests/test_skip_defaults.py tests/test_response_by_alias.py` → 59 passed, 1 skipped.

Related: discussions #16029 (original report) and #15961.

title: Type annotation mismatch in sub-dependencies example (query_extractor may return None)
body:
### Privileged issue

- [x] I'm @tiangolo or he asked me directly to create an issue here.

### Issue Content

Hi! First of all, thank you for the excellent documentation.

I noticed what appears to be a type annotation inconsistency in the **"Use the dependency"** example:

https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/sub-dependencies/#use-the-dependency

The first dependency is defined as:

```python
def query_extractor(q: str | None = None):
    return q
```

Since `q` is annotated as `str | None`, this function can return either a `str` or `None`.

Later, its return value is injected into the `q` parameter of another dependency:

```python
def query_or_cookie_extractor(
    q: Annotated[str, Depends(query_extractor)],
    last_query: Annotated[str | None, Cookie()] = None,
):
    if not q:
        return last_query
    return q
```

Here, `q` is annotated as `str`, but `query_extractor()` may return `None`.

For example, if a request is made without the `q` query parameter:

```http
GET /items/
```

then FastAPI will effectively resolve the dependencies like this:

```python
query_extractor(q=None)
# returns None

query_or_cookie_extractor(
    q=None,
    last_query=...
)
```

In other words, `q` may actually receive `None` at runtime, even though it is annotated as `str`.

The implementation itself seems to acknowledge this possibility:

```python
if not q:
    return last_query
```

This condition would only be necessary if `q` could be missing, empty, or `None`.

Because of that, wouldn't the following annotation be more accurate?

```python
def query_or_cookie_extractor(
    q: Annotated[str | None, Depends(query_extractor)],
    last_query: Annotated[str | None, Cookie()] = None,
):
    if not q:
        return last_query
    return q
```

This would make the type annotation consistent with the actual return type of the dependency and may help avoid confusion for users learning dependency injection or using static type checkers.

If there is an intentional reason for annotating `q` as `str`, I would appreciate any clarification.

Thanks again for the great documentation!

title: Fix Pydantic Header model field alias resolution & transport header validation
body:
### Summary
This PR addresses two edge cases when extracting request headers via Pydantic `BaseModel` annotations (`headers: Annotated[HeaderModel, Header()]`):

1. **Header Alias Case Normalization**: Starlette normalizes incoming HTTP header names to lower-case (e.g. `x-custom-auth`), whereas `processed_keys` previously only tracked the exact mixed-case alias string (`X-Custom-Auth`). When `extra="forbid"` was set on the model, valid header inputs were incorrectly marked as `extra_forbidden`.
2. **Client Transport Header Filtering**: Standard HTTP protocol headers attached automatically by clients/servers (`Host`, `User-Agent`, `Accept`, `Accept-Encoding`, `Connection`) were passed into model validation dictionaries, causing validation failures on strict header models.

### Solution
- Lowercased and hyphenated field aliases and validation aliases are now registered in `processed_keys` during `Headers` parameter extraction.
- Standard HTTP transport headers are filtered out when extracting a Header model configured with `extra="forbid"`.
- Added new unit test file `tests/test_header_model_alias_bug.py`.

### Tests & Verification
Ran `pytest` across all header test suites (`141 passed in 1.94s`):
- `tests/test_header_model_alias_bug.py`
- `tests/test_query_cookie_header_model_extra_params.py`

title: Fix UnboundLocalError in OpenAPI generation for custom response classes
body:
## Problem

In `get_openapi_path` (`fastapi/openapi/utils.py`), `status_code` is assigned **only inside** the branches, then used unconditionally as a dict key:

```python
if route.status_code is not None:
    status_code = str(route.status_code)
else:
    response_signature = inspect.signature(current_response_class.__init__)
    status_code_param = response_signature.parameters.get("status_code")
    if status_code_param is not None:
        if isinstance(status_code_param.default, int):
            status_code = str(status_code_param.default)
operation.setdefault("responses", {}).setdefault(status_code, {})["description"] = route.response_description
```

When `route.status_code is None` **and** the response class's `__init__` has no `status_code` parameter (or its default isn't an `int`), `status_code` is never bound → `UnboundLocalError` on the `setdefault(status_code, ...)` line.

## Impact

`get_openapi_path` → `get_openapi` → `Application.openapi()`, so this doesn't just affect one route — it crashes **the whole schema generation**, taking down `/openapi.json`, `/docs`, and `/redoc` for the entire app.

It's reachable with a common wrapper pattern: a custom `response_class` whose `__init__` is `def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs)` (or types `status_code` as `int | None = None`).

## Reproduction

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

class MyResponse(JSONResponse):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/x", response_class=MyResponse)
def x():
    return {"a": 1}

app.openapi()   # before: UnboundLocalError at openapi/utils.py; after: works
```

## Fix

Bind a fallback (`"200"`, FastAPI's default route status) before the branches so `status_code` is always defined. The existing (working) paths are unchanged — they still overwrite it.

```python
status_code = "200"
if route.status_code is not None:
    ...
```

title: 🐛 Fix `Form()` with an `Optional` Pydantic model silently discarding submitted data
body:
### Bug

A form body parameter typed as `Optional[SomeModel]` (`SomeModel | None`) silently drops the submitted fields and resolves to `None` with **no validation error** — while the equivalent JSON body parses correctly. Simply adding `| None` to an otherwise-working `Annotated[SomeModel, Form()]` parameter breaks it.

```python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from pydantic import BaseModel

class UserForm(BaseModel):
    username: str

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/x")
def x(data: Annotated[UserForm | None, Form()] = None):
    return data

# POST /x  with form field  username=alice  ->  returns null  (data silently lost)
# The same endpoint with Annotated[UserForm, Form()] returns {"username": "alice"}
```

### Cause

`is_union_of_base_models()` returns `False` for `SomeModel | None` because `NoneType` is not a `BaseModel` subclass. That makes `_should_embed_body_fields()` force-embed the field, so the top-level form fields are never expanded into the model and the value falls back to the default (`None`). The `None` member case was not considered when this helper was introduced in #13827 (`tests/test_union_forms.py` only covered `UserForm | CompanyForm`).

### Fix

Ignore `None` members when checking a union of models, so `Optional[SomeModel]` (and `A | B | None`) keeps being treated as a top-level model union. An empty form still validates the required fields (a `422`), which is consistent with how an empty JSON `{}` body behaves.

### Tests

Added regression tests to `tests/test_union_forms.py` covering the required, defaulted, and multi-member-union optional cases, and updated the OpenAPI snapshot (which now correctly shows `anyOf: [SomeModel, {"type": "null"}]`).

title: Optimize APIRoute handler caching and fix endpoint context cache
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes two issues in `routing.py`:

1. Cache the generated request handler for effective route contexts to avoid rebuilding it on every request.
2. Replace the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with a `WeakKeyDictionary` to avoid stale cache entries and allow unused entries to be garbage-collected.

## Motivation

While reviewing `routing.py`, I noticed that routes using an effective route context rebuild their request handler on every incoming request, even though the effective context itself is already cached and stable. Caching the generated ASGI application avoids repeating the same work and reduces unnecessary allocations.

I also noticed that `_endpoint_context_cache` is keyed by `id(func)`. Since object IDs may be reused after an object is garbage-collected, this can theoretically return stale endpoint metadata. Additionally, the cache never shrinks because entries remain for the lifetime of the process. Using `WeakKeyDictionary` avoids both issues.

## Changes

- Added lazy caching of the generated ASGI application on `_EffectiveRouteContext`.
- Reused the cached application for subsequent requests.
- Replaced the `id()`-based endpoint context cache with `weakref.WeakKeyDictionary`.
- Added a fallback for callables that cannot be weak-referenced by computing the context without caching.

## Expected Impact

- Reduces repeated request handler construction.
- Avoids unnecessary allocations on repeated requests.
- Eliminates potential stale cache lookups caused by `id()` reuse.
- Prevents unbounded growth of the endpoint context cache.
- Preserves existing behavior while improving efficiency.

## Related Discussion

Related to: #discussion-10445342

## Testing

- Added tests covering the new behavior.
- Verified that the existing test suite passes.
- Confirmed that routing behavior remains unchanged while exercising the modified code paths.

### Discussed in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/15979
Originally posted by **UditDewan** July 12, 2026 ### First Check - [x] I added a very descriptive title here. - [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [x] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [x] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [x] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [x] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Pydantic. - [x] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to Swagger UI. - [x] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to ReDoc. ### Commit to Help - [x] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python import os import tempfile from fastapi import FastAPI from fastapi.testclient import TestClient dist = tempfile.mkdtemp() with open(os.path.join(dist, "index.html"), "w") as f: f.write("SPA shell") app = FastAPI() app.frontend("/", directory=dist, fallback="index.html") client = TestClient(app) # The Accept header a browser sends on a normal top level navigation. browser_nav = { "accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9," "image/avif,image/webp,image/apng,*/*;q=0.8" } print(client.get("/users/john", headers=browser_nav).status_code) # 200, serves index.html print(client.get("/users/john.doe", headers=browser_nav).status_code) # 404 print(client.get("/v/1.2.3", headers=browser_nav).status_code) # 404 ``` ### Description Hi 👋 I have been trying out the new `app.frontend()` helper to serve a single page app, using `fallback="index.html"` so that client side routes fall back to the shell and the frontend router can take over. This is the behavior described in the "Client side routing" part of the docs, and it works fine for a path like `/dashboard` or `/dashboard/settings`. The problem shows up when a client side route has a dot in its last path segment. Plenty of real apps have these, for example a profile at `/users/john.doe`, a version deep link at `/v/1.2.3`, or a slug like `/files/report.2024`. When I open one of those directly, or just hit refresh while I am already on that page, I get a 404 instead of the `index.html` shell, so the app never loads and the client router never gets a chance to handle the route. The part that surprised me is that setting `fallback="index.html"` explicitly does not change this. As far as I can tell there is currently no way to get these routes to fall back to the shell. I spent some time reading the code and I think it comes from `_is_frontend_navigation_request()` in `fastapi/routing.py`. It takes the last path segment and if `os.path.splitext(...)` finds an extension it returns early and treats the request as an asset request, before it ever looks at the `Accept` header. Because `os.path.splitext("john.doe")` returns `.doe`, any segment with a dot in it is treated as a file and never gets the `index.html` fallback, even when the browser clearly asked for `text/html`. What makes me think this is fixable without regressions is that the two situations are easy to tell apart. A real browser navigation sends `Accept: text/html`, while a missing asset requested from a script tag, an image tag, or a fetch call sends `*/*` or a specific type like `text/css`. If I request a genuinely missing asset such as `/assets/missing.js` with `Accept: */*` it still returns 404 as expected, so checking the `Accept` header first would fix the navigation case and keep the asset case working. I did notice there is already a test that pins the current behavior. `test_index_fallback_does_not_handle_asset_like_or_non_html_requests` has a `("/users/jane.doe", "text/html")` case that expects a 404, so before proposing a change I wanted to ask whether the current behavior is intentional. If the idea is that dotted client routes should be servable, would a change that treats an explicit `Accept: text/html` request as navigation regardless of the path be acceptable? Or would you rather keep the extension heuristic as the default for `fallback="auto"` and add an opt in for apps that use dotted client side routes? I am happy to open a PR with a failing test and the change for whichever direction you prefer. Thanks a lot for the work on this feature. ### Operating System Windows ### Operating System Details Also reproduced on current master. The logic involved is pure routing code, so it is not tied to any particular operating system. ### FastAPI Version 0.139.0 ### Pydantic Version 2.13.4 ### Python Version 3.11 ### Additional Context _No response_

title: Fix broken relative links in translated docs
body:
I noticed while looking at the translated documentation that there are three relative links that point to pages that are only in English. This results in 404s for users visiting the docs in any other locale than English.

What's broken
Affected files and links are:

docs//docs/deployment/versions.md — links to ../release-notes.md, which doesn't exist in any translated locale
docs//docs/help-fastapi.md — links to newsletter.md and fastapi-people.md#fastapi-experts, which are not translated.
This impacts all 12 locales that are translated (de, es, fr, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, zh-hant).

What I changed
Replaced broken relative links with absolute links to the English pages:

Old = ../release-notes.md
mew = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/

old = newsletter.md
new = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/newsletter/

old = fastapi-people.md#fastapi-experts
new = https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/fastapi-people/#fastapi-experts

Why absolute URLs
These pages (release-notes, newsletter, fastapi-people) are only maintained in English. It's a good idea to use absolute URLs here, as they will not silently fail if the page is renamed, and they will properly redirect translated users to the English version of the page, instead of a broken link. This is in line with other untranslated cross-references in the docs.

title: fix: pass include/exclude/custom_encoder in jsonable_encoder BaseModel recursive call
body:
Summary: When jsonable_encoder receives a BaseModel instance, it calls obj.model_dump() then makes a recursive call that silently drops custom_encoder, include, exclude, by_alias, and exclude_unset. The dataclass branch correctly passes all these parameters.

Verification:
- Not dead code: jsonable_encoder is called from serialize_response and is a documented public API.
- The existing test_custom_encoders test uses a TypedDict, not a BaseModel.
- custom_encoder is clearly a bug - it cannot affect nested values inside a BaseModel with the current code.

title: fix: use None sentinel instead of mutable OAuthFlowsModel() default in OAuth2.__init__
body:
## Summary

`OAuth2.__init__` uses `OAuthFlowsModel()` as a mutable default argument. Every call to `OAuth2()` without explicit `flows` shares the same `OAuthFlowsModel` instance. Mutations to that instance propagate across all default-using instances.

Changed to `None` sentinel with `if flows is None: flows = OAuthFlowsModel()` inside the function body.

## Verification
- Called whenever OAuth2 is instantiated without explicit flows.
- Consistent with how `SecurityScopes` (same file, line 666) handles scopes defaults.

title: fix: pass include/exclude/by_alias params to jsonable_encoder when no response_model
body:
## Summary

`serialize_response` receives `include`, `exclude`, `by_alias`, `exclude_unset`, `exclude_defaults`, and `exclude_none` parameters. When `field` is None (no `response_model`), it calls `jsonable_encoder(response_content)` without passing any of those filtering parameters. They are silently ignored.

A user who writes `@app.get("/items", response_model_include={"name", "id"})` without a `response_model` would expect the exclude to work, but it doesn't.

## Verification
- Not dead code: called on every non-streaming endpoint response when no response_model is set.
- All existing tests pair `response_model_include`/`response_model_exclude` with `response_model`.

title: Restore PEP 740 release attestations (lost in the uv migration)
body:
Hi — thanks for FastAPI.

I noticed the published wheels lost their signed provenance in the switch to `uv`, and I don't think it was intended. Checking PyPI's integrity API:

| version | uploaded | `/integrity/.../provenance` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.127.0 | 2025-12-21 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| 0.128.0 | 2025-12-27 | HTTP 200 — signed |
| **0.129.0** | 2026-02-12 | **HTTP 404 — none** |
| 0.139.0 (latest) | 2026-07-01 | HTTP 404 — none |

The first release without provenance is the first one after `⬆️ Migrate to uv (#14676)`. That commit replaced `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` (which emits PEP 740 attestations by default for Trusted Publishing projects) with `uv publish`, and uv's docs note it *"does not currently generate attestations."* The Trusted Publishing identity (`id-token: write`) is still configured, so it looks like only the emission step was dropped, silently — nothing fails in CI when attestations stop being produced, which is probably why it went unnoticed.

This PR keeps `uv build` and hands the upload back to `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, which restores attestation emission. It's the one step, nothing else changes.

For a quick sanity check that the action still attests under Trusted Publishing: `huggingface/transformers` publishes this way and its wheels carry provenance today (`https://pypi.org/integrity/transformers/5.13.1/transformers-5.13.1-py3-none-any.whl/provenance` → 200).

I may be missing a reason `uv publish` was preferred here — if so, please just close this, no problem at all. If you'd rather keep `uv publish` and generate the attestations separately before upload, that works too; happy to adjust.

<sub>I used an AI assistant to trace this and prepare the change; it's credited in the commit trailer. I verified every step myself.</sub>

title: 🐛 Fix race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild under concurrent first requests
body:
Fixes #15974. Also reported in discussion #15914.

## Problem

`_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates()` and `_IncludedRouter.effective_low_priority_routes()` rebuild their cached lists lazily with no synchronization. The rebuild publishes an empty list on the shared attribute before filling it and stamps the version afterwards. When several threads send the app's first requests concurrently (per-thread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any setup that serves one app object from multiple event loops), multiple threads pass the version check and append into the same list. The cache ends up permanently holding duplicated candidates (around 600 entries for a 120 route app in the repro), a concurrent reader can see a partially built list and 404 a valid route, and the interleaved `warnings.catch_warnings()` calls inside the rebuild can leak global warnings filters.

## Fix

Guard the rebuild with a per-instance lock and double-checked version test, build the new list into a local variable, and publish it atomically (list first, version second). Readers on the fast path never see a partial list, concurrent first requests trigger exactly one rebuild, and the warnings filter state is no longer touched by interleaved rebuilds of the same router.

The lock field is excluded from the dataclass `repr` and `eq` so existing semantics are unchanged.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_included_router_concurrent_rebuild.py`, which fires the first requests from several threads through a barrier and asserts that all requests succeed and that the cache holds exactly one candidate per route. It fails on master and passes with this change. All existing router and include tests pass.

title: Race condition in _IncludedRouter cache rebuild can 404 valid routes and permanently corrupt the candidate cache
body:
### Description

Since the router refactor in 0.137.0 (#15745), `_IncludedRouter.effective_candidates()` and `_IncludedRouter.effective_low_priority_routes()` in `fastapi/routing.py` rebuild their cached lists lazily on first use, with no synchronization.

The rebuild publishes an empty list on the shared attribute first, appends routes into it one by one, and only stamps the version at the end:

```python
self._effective_candidates = []
# ... appends into self._effective_candidates in a loop ...
self._effective_candidates_version = routes_version
```

If several threads drive the app's first requests at the same time (for example per-thread `TestClient`s in a parallel test suite, or any embedding that serves one app object from multiple event loops), more than one thread can pass the version check and rebuild concurrently. Every rebuilder appends into whichever list was assigned to the attribute last, so the cache ends up with duplicated candidates, and the corruption is permanent because the version gets stamped anyway. A request that runs while the list is still partially built can also get a 404 for a route that exists.

The rebuild path additionally uses `warnings.catch_warnings()` internally (via response field construction), so interleaved rebuilds can leak entries into the global warnings filters.

### Reproduction

```python
import sys
import threading

from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI
from fastapi.routing import _IncludedRouter
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

N_ROUTES = 120
N_THREADS = 6

app = FastAPI()
router = APIRouter()
for i in range(N_ROUTES):
    def endpoint(i: int = i):
        return {"i": i}
    router.add_api_route(f"/r{i}", endpoint, methods=["GET"])
app.include_router(router)

sys.setswitchinterval(1e-5)  # widen the rebuild window
barrier = threading.Barrier(N_THREADS)

def worker():
    client = TestClient(app)
    barrier.wait()
    client.get(f"/r{N_ROUTES - 1}")

threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(N_THREADS)]
for t in threads:
    t.start()
for t in threads:
    t.join()

included = next(r for r in app.router.routes if isinstance(r, _IncludedRouter))
print(len(included._effective_candidates), "cached candidates, expected", N_ROUTES)
```

On my machine this reliably prints around 600 cached candidates for the 120 route app.

### Expected behavior

The cache rebuild should be thread safe. Building the list into a local variable and publishing it atomically (list first, version second) keeps readers from ever seeing a partial list, and serializing the rebuild avoids the duplicated appends and the warnings filter leak.

### Environment

- FastAPI version: 0.139.0
- Python version: 3.14.5
- OS: Windows 11

Related report: discussion #15914 describes the same symptoms.
